Analyze the architecture and working of IoMT systems in 
healthcare applications.

2B

Ans 
The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is a network of 
interconnected medical devices, sensors, software applications, and 
healthcare systems that collect, transmit, process, and analyze 
patient health data. The architecture of an IoMT system typically 
consists of three main layers: the Data Collection Layer, Data 
Management Layer, and Medical Server/Application Layer. 
The Data Collection Layer includes wearable devices, biosensors, 
and monitoring equipment that gather physiological data such as 
heart rate, blood pressure, ECG, temperature, and oxygen 
saturation. This data is transmitted through communication 
technologies such as Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, ZigBee, or 5G to the Data 
Management Layer, where it is stored, organized, filtered, and 
secured. The processed data is then forwarded to the Medical Server 
Layer, which performs advanced analytics, supports clinical 
decision-making, generates alerts, and enables remote patient 
monitoring. In healthcare applications, IoMT facilitates real-time 
health tracking, telemedicine, early disease detection, and 
personalized treatment, thereby improving patient outcomes, 
reducing healthcare costs, and enhancing the efficiency of 
healthcare delivery systems.

secure routing protocols, VPNs, TLS/DTLS encryption, and 
firewalls to prevent eavesdropping and MITM attacks during 
transmission. 
c) Edge/Fog Layer 
Local processing units (edge servers) perform preliminary data 
filtering and analytics closer to the source, reducing latency. 
Security here includes edge-based intrusion detection and local 
access control policies.

(ABAC) Engine 
• 
Design: Access decisions based on

o Role (doctor, nurse, patient, admin) 
o Department (cardiology, general

o Nurse + General Ward → Access to 
basic vitals only, no diagnostic 
history. 
o Patient → Access to own data only, 
read-only. 
o Cloud Provider → Access to 
anonymized data only, for analytics 
purposes. 
• 
Justification: ABAC provides fine-grained, 
context-aware access control superior to 
simple role-based systems, critical in

• 
Design: Every request—even from within 
the hospital network—is authenticated and 
authorized before granting access. No 
implicit trust based on network location.

Components:  
o Micro-segmentation: IoMT devices 
isolated into secure network zones. 
o Continuous verification: Session 
tokens re-validated periodically 
during active use. 
• 
Justification: Prevents lateral movement of 
attackers even if one device/credential is 
compromised.

Access Ledger 
• 
Design: Every access request and grant is 
recorded on a permissioned blockchain (e.g., 
Hyperledger Fabric), including patient 
consent status.

Justification: Provides an immutable, 
transparent audit trail, ensuring compliance 
with regulations (HIPAA/GDPR) and 
enabling patients to track who accessed their 
data.

Integration

Design: All cloud service provider access 
routed through an API gateway using OAuth 
2.0 with scoped tokens (limited permissions, 
time-bound). 
• 
Justification: Prevents third-party providers 
from having broad, unrestricted access to 
sensitive patient data.
